BiblicalUsage: Zedad was a town on the northern border of the promised land, named when God drew the boundary for Israel and again when Ezekiel saw the borders of the restored land. It marks the edge of the inheritance, where the land of promise meets the land beyond. It is named twice, both times as a border.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God draws the borders of His promises, and Zedad is one of the marks on the line. The inheritance is measured, and every marker is placed by Him.
